mcqs.question: A right circular cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm is attached to the base of a right circular cone of the same radius and height 5 cm. What is the total exposed surface area of the combined solid?
mcqs.explanation: The hidden face is the common circular base of radius 3 cm. Exposed area = cylinder curved (2πrh = 60π) + cylinder bottom (πr² = 9π) + cone curved (πrl, l = √(r²+h²) = √34, so π·3·√34 = 3π√34). Total = 60π + 9π + 3π√34 ≈ 271.7 cm² ≈ 272 cm². Options B, C, D either add the hidden area or omit parts, showing the common misconception of counting hidden surfaces.

mcqs.question: A rectangular prism measures 8 cm × 6 cm × 10 cm. A hemisphere of radius 3 cm is placed on the top face (8 cm × 6 cm). What is the total volume of the resulting solid?
mcqs.explanation: Volume = volume of prism + volume of hemisphere. Prism: 8×6×10 = 480 cm³. Hemisphere: (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π·27 = 18π ≈ 56.55 cm³. Total ≈ 480 + 56.55 = 536.55 cm³ ≈ 536.5 cm³. The other options ignore one part or over‑estimate.

mcqs.learning_point: Avoid counting hidden surfaces when finding exposed area
mcqs.question: Solid A: a cube of side 4 cm with a square pyramid (base 4 cm × 4 cm, height 6 cm) attached on its top face. Solid B: a cube of side 4 cm with a rectangular prism (4 cm × 4 cm × 6 cm) attached on its top face. Which solid has the larger total exposed surface area?

options.C: Both have the same exposed area
options.D: Cannot be determined without more information

mcqs.explanation:
For both solids the top face of the cube (16 cm²) is hidden. 
Solid A: Exposed area = 5 cube faces (5×16 = 80) + pyramid lateral area. Lateral area = (1/2)·perimeter·slant height = 8·6.3249 ≈ 50.6 cm². Total ≈ 130.6 cm².
Solid B: Prism total SA = 2(ab+bc+ac) = 128 cm²; hidden face = 16 cm², so exposed prism area = 112 cm². Adding the 5 cube faces (80 cm²) gives ≈ 192 cm², which is larger. Hence Solid B has the greater exposed area. The comparison tests the ability to exclude hidden faces correctly.

mcqs.question: A water tank consists of a right circular cylinder of radius 5 m and height 12 m, closed at the bottom and topped with a hemispherical dome. What is the total external surface area that needs to be painted (excluding the base of the cylinder)?
mcqs.explanation: Painted area = curved surface of cylinder + curved surface of hemisphere. Cylinder curved area = 2πrh = 2π·5·12 = 120π. Hemisphere curved area = 2πr² = 2π·25 = 50π. Total = 170π ≈ 534.07 m² ≈ 534 m². Options B‑D either add the base or use wrong formulas.

mcqs.question: A solid is formed by joining a right circular cone (base radius 4 cm, height 9 cm) to the top of a right circular cylinder (radius 4 cm, height 12 cm). Which component solids constitute this composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: The description mentions a cylinder and a cone attached together; no other solid is involved. Hence the components are a cylinder and a cone. Options A and B list only one component, and D mentions a sphere which is not present.

mcqs.question: A cube of side 6 cm has a square pyramid (base 6 cm × 6 cm, height 5 cm) attached to its top face. What is the total exposed surface area of the resulting solid?
mcqs.explanation: Exposed cube faces = 5 × 6² = 5 × 36 = 180 cm² (top face is hidden). Pyramid lateral area = (1/2)·perimeter·slant height. Perimeter = 4·6 = 24 cm. Slant height = √[(3)² + 5²] = √34 ≈ 5.830 cm. Lateral area = 0.5·24·5.830 = 12·5.830 ≈ 69.96 cm². Total exposed area ≈ 180 + 69.96 ≈ 249.96 ≈ 250 cm². The other options miss either the pyramid area or the hidden face.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the volume of a composite solid?

options.A: It is the sum of the volumes of the individual solids minus the volume of any overlapping region.
options.B: It is the sum of the surface areas of the individual solids.
options.C: It is the product of the lengths of its three dimensions.
options.D: It is equal only to the volume of the larger component solid.

mcqs.answer: It is the sum of the volumes of the individual solids minus the volume of any overlapping region.
mcqs.explanation: The volume of a composite solid is obtained by adding the volumes of all constituent solids and subtracting any part that is counted twice because of overlap. Option B confuses volume with surface area, C describes a rectangular prism only, and D ignores the contribution of the smaller solid.

mcqs.learning_point: Avoid counting hidden surfaces when finding exposed area
mcqs.question: A rectangular block of dimensions 6 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm has a hemisphere of radius 3 cm attached to one of its 6 cm × 6 cm faces. What is the total exposed surface area of the combined solid?
mcqs.explanation: Block total SA = 2(ab+bc+ac) = 2(36+24+24) = 168 cm². The face where the hemisphere is attached (area 36 cm²) is hidden, so exposed block area = 168 – 36 = 132 cm². Hemisphere curved area = 2πr² = 2π·9 = 18π ≈ 56.55 cm². Total exposed area ≈ 132 + 56.55 ≈ 188.55 cm² ≈ 189 cm². Options B, C, D either ignore the hidden face or the hemisphere’s curved area.
